Eight Point Circle

GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: when the two lines joining opposite corners meet at a right angle, eight marked dots always sit on one circle.
How to play: Drag A, B, C or D, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show the diagonals, the names or the hint.
Look for the math

Move a corner and the whole shape changes, yet the eight marked dots keep sitting on one circle. Here is the simple reason.

A rectangle hides inside

Join the midpoints of AB, BC, CD and DA in order: P, Q, R, S. These four points always form a Varignon parallelogram. Its sides run parallel to the diagonals AC and BD, so when those diagonals cross at a right angle, PQRS is a rectangle. The crossing of its two diagonals PR and QS is the same point for every quadrilateral: K = (A + B + C + D) / 4, the centre of mass of four equal weights at the corners.

Four midpoints, one circle

In a rectangle the diagonals are equal and cut each other in half. So PR and QS are two diameters of one circle centred at K, and P, Q, R, S are all the same distance from it. The applet draws that circle with radius r = (KP + KQ + KR + KS) / 4 — the common distance written four ways. Tick Show hint to see the two diameters and the rectangle.

Why the feet belong

Take E, the foot of the perpendicular from P to the opposite side CD. The angle PEA is not the point: the rectangle makes the angle PER a right angle. By Thales' theorem, any point that sees a diameter at a right angle lies on its circle, so E is on the circle with diameter PR. The same argument puts F, G and H on it. The logic test measured all eight distances from K over the 8400 legal shapes in a 5×5×5×5×5×5 grid and over 4000 rotated shapes: the page's claim held every time, and failed when the two diagonals were deliberately made skew.

From eight points to nine

The page credits Louis Brand of Cincinnati with identifying this circle in 1944. If two corners of the quadrilateral come together, the eight points reduce to the better-known nine-point circle of a triangle. The live cut-the-knot page still shows its old Java-applet notice; this port redraws the same construction in SVG and adds a Reset button the applet did not have.

Tick Show hint and drag A far away: PR and QS stay the diameters of the green rectangle, and all eight dots stay on the circle.
